title: Do as you choose
hookLine: after seven hundred verses, Krishna hands the decision back to Arjuna
carry: god teaches, then trusts you to choose
tomorrow: "Abandon all dharmas, come to me alone" (18.66–18.72)

cards: Think of everything Arjuna has been given on that chariot. Seventeen chapters of answers. Once, a vision of Krishna's universal form so overwhelming that he begged to see the gentle form again.

Out on the field, the armies are still waiting for one man to lift his bow or lay it down. Now, at the very end, Krishna could simply say: fight. Instead, he closes the teaching and hands the decision back.

teach.b: It starts with a warning. Verse fifty-nine: if, leaning on your ego, you think, I will not fight, that decision is useless. Your own nature will push you to it.
Verse sixty: bound by your own work, born of your nature, you'll do helplessly what you, confused, don't want to do.
Then verse sixty-one, a strange picture: the Lord lives in the heart of every being, Arjuna, and by his power moves them all, as if they were mounted on a machine.
Verse sixty-two: go to him for refuge with your whole being; by his grace you'll reach the highest peace. Then verse sixty-three. I have told you this wisdom, more secret than any secret.

teach.h: REFLECT, THEN DO AS YOU WISH.
teach.b: Then do as you wish. Yathecchasi tatha kuru. As you wish, so do.

After all the teaching, all the argument, the vision of chapter eleven, Krishna doesn't force a choice. The Gita's God persuades, shows, loves, and then respects Arjuna enough to let him decide. But he doesn't walk away.
Verse sixty-four: hear my highest word once more.
You are deeply loved by me. Verse sixty-five repeats a line from chapter nine: keep your mind on me, be devoted to me, and you will come to me.
I promise you truly, for you are dear to me. So the handing back isn't cold. It comes wrapped in the plainest statement of love in the whole book.
Many teachers see a deep Hindu idea here: the Lord lives in every heart, and still the choice is put in human hands.
And it closes the week: om tat sat, letting go of the fruit, five causes, the gunas, your own dharma, the road to Brahman, and now this.

how: Hindu teachers often point to Gita 18.63, 'reflect fully, then do as you wish', as a sign that the Gita invites understanding and free choice rather than blind obedience.

o: as you wish: the choice is left to you
as I command: do exactly what I say
as fate decides: what's written will happen

games.q: you're Krishna. you've taught for seventeen chapters and shown Arjuna your cosmic form. how do you finish?
o: tell him to reflect fully, then do as he wishes.
games.why: reflect fully, then do as you wish (18.63), followed at once by: you are deeply loved by me (18.64).

practice: Bring to mind one choice you're facing. If you pray, bring it to God first, as verse sixty-two invites. Let all the advice you've been given about it, from people, from books, from these days, be said once; then let it go quiet.
In the quiet, reflect on it fully, the way verse sixty-three asks. You don't have to decide; just notice that the choice is yours, and that you can make it without fear.

wordCard.voice: Yathecchasi, as you wish. Gita eighteen, sixty-three: after all the teaching, Krishna says reflect fully, then do as you wish, yathecchasi tatha kuru.

orig.note: Sanskrit: yathecchasi tatha kuru, as you wish, so do; the end of Gita 18.63.

carryVoice: Your line: God teaches, then trusts you to choose. And you are deeply loved. That's day two hundred twenty-four.
